title: Nashville Hot Honey Chicken Thighs
blurb: Craggy shallow-fried thighs lacquered in a cayenne-and-hot-honey paste that soaks straight into the crust, served the only correct way: on white bread with pickles.

ingredients.item: 2 slices L'Oven Fresh white sandwich bread

steps.text: Halve the thighs into rough 3-inch pieces, season them hard with salt and pepper, then toss with the buttermilk in a bowl until every piece is coated. Let them sit while you set up the dredge.
steps.tip: Even a short soak seasons the meat through.

steps.text: Whisk the flour with 1 tsp of the cayenne, 1 tsp of the smoked paprika, the garlic powder, and a big pinch of salt in a shallow dish. Drizzle in 2 tbsp of the buttermilk from the bowl and rake it with a fork so the flour turns shaggy and pebbly.
steps.tip: Those flour clumps become the crunchy bits.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a 10-inch cast iron or heavy skillet over medium-high until it reaches about 350F, or until a pinch of flour sizzles briskly on contact. Press each thigh piece firmly into the dredge on both sides, then lay it in the oil away from you.
steps.tip: Crowding drops the oil temperature fast.

steps.text: Fry in two batches without moving the chicken until the underside is deep mahogany and releases on its own, then flip and fry the second side until the crust is crisp and the thickest piece hits 175F.
steps.tip: Adjust heat to keep a steady, lively sizzle.

steps.text: Move the fried chicken to a rack set over a plate so the bottom crust stays crisp. Carefully spoon 3 tbsp of the hot frying oil into a heatproof bowl and discard the rest.
steps.tip: Frying oil is the flavor base for the paste.

steps.text: Whisk the remaining cayenne and smoked paprika, the brown sugar, and the hot honey into that reserved hot oil until it turns glossy and brick red. Taste it on a pickle and add more cayenne if you want it truly hot.
steps.tip: The heat of the oil blooms the spices.

steps.text: Brush the paste generously over both sides of the chicken and let it soak in while you lay the bread on two plates. Pile the chicken on the bread, top with pickle chips, and drizzle any paste left in the bowl over the top.
steps.tip: The bread is a sponge, not a side.

swap: No buttermilk? Thin 1/3 cup Friendly Farms Greek yogurt with 3 tbsp water and use that instead.
leftovers: Refrigerate the chicken uncovered on a rack for up to 3 days and reheat at 400F for 8 minutes to bring the crust back.

title: Sambal Balado Shrimp with Coconut Jasmine Rice
blurb: Sweet-salty kecap manis and a slick of chili crunch cling to fat red shrimp, spooned over jasmine rice cooked with coconut milk until it smells like a beach.

ingredients.item: 1 lb Raw Argentinian Red Shrimp, thawed and patted dry
1 red bell pepper, cut in thin strips

steps.text: Stir the soy sauce and brown sugar together in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves into a syrupy kecap manis. Set it next to the stove along with the chili onion crunch.
steps.tip: Have everything at arm's reach; this cooks fast.

steps.text: Microwave the jasmine rice packets according to the package, then tip the hot rice into a bowl and fold in the coconut milk and a big pinch of salt. Cover and leave it alone so the rice drinks the coconut milk.
steps.tip: It should look creamy, not soupy.

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high until it shimmers, then add the shallots and bell pepper. Stir-fry until the shallot edges are browned and the peppers are blistered but still snappy.
steps.tip: High heat, constant motion.

steps.text: Push the vegetables to one side, add the garlic to the bare spot, and stir it in the oil until fragrant and just turning pale gold. Do not let it go past blond or the whole pan turns bitter.
steps.tip: Garlic burns in seconds at this heat.

steps.text: Season the shrimp with salt, spread them in a single layer, and leave them undisturbed until the bottoms turn opaque orange. Flip once and cook until they curl into loose Cs.
steps.tip: Tight O-shaped shrimp are overcooked.

steps.text: Pour in the kecap manis mixture and the chili onion crunch, then toss hard for 30 seconds until the sauce reduces to a glaze that coats every shrimp and slides off the spoon slowly.
steps.tip: Kill the heat the moment it turns glossy.

steps.text: Squeeze half the lime over the pan, scoop the coconut rice into two bowls, and spoon the shrimp and all the pan sauce over the top. Finish with cilantro and the remaining lime in wedges.

swap: Out of Crunchy Chili Onion? Use 2 tbsp Fusia sriracha plus 1 tbsp oil and a spoonful of crispy fried onions.
leftovers: Store shrimp and rice separately for up to 2 days and reheat the shrimp in a hot skillet for 1 minute so they don't turn rubbery.

title: Piri-Piri Chicken with Smoky Sausage and Peppers
blurb: Thin chicken cutlets get a vinegary chile-and-smoked-paprika lashing, seared in the rendered fat of smoked sausage and finished with charred peppers and lemon.

ingredients.item: 1 1/4 lb Simply Nature Organic Chicken Breasts, sliced into thin cutlets
6 oz Never Any! smoked sausage, cut in coins

steps.text: Whisk the harissa, smoked paprika, pepper flakes, garlic, vinegar, 3 tbsp olive oil, and 1 tsp salt into a loose piri-piri sauce. Spoon half of it over the chicken cutlets and turn them until slick; reserve the rest for finishing.
steps.tip: Thin cutlets take on marinade fast.

steps.text: Set a large skillet over medium heat and lay in the sausage coins in a single layer. Cook until the edges are browned and curled and a shallow layer of orange fat has rendered out, then scoop the sausage onto a plate and leave the fat behind.
steps.tip: That rendered fat is your searing medium.

steps.text: Raise the heat to medium-high and let the pan get hot enough that a drop of water skitters. Lay the cutlets in without crowding and press them flat with a spatula.
steps.tip: Work in two batches if the pan is tight.

steps.text: Sear undisturbed until the underside is deeply browned and the marinade has caramelized at the edges, then flip and cook until the center is just firm and the juices run clear.
steps.tip: Thin cutlets go from done to dry quickly.

steps.text: Move the chicken to a board to rest. Add the frozen peppers and onions straight to the hot pan and spread them out, letting them sit still so the water cooks off and the edges char.
steps.tip: Don't stir for the first few minutes.

steps.text: Return the sausage to the pan, add the juices from the chicken board, and squeeze in half the lemon. Toss for a minute until everything is glossy and smells sharp and smoky.

Slice the chicken thick against the grain and pile it over the peppers right in the skillet. Spoon the reserved piri-piri over the top, scatter parsley, and serve with torn ciabatta for mopping and lemon wedges.
steps.tip: The raw sauce at the end is the whole point.

swap: No Harissa on hand? Use 2 tbsp Burman's chimichurri hot sauce plus an extra teaspoon of smoked paprika.
leftovers: Chop everything together and refrigerate up to 3 days; it makes an outstanding filling for a ciabatta sandwich with a smear of the leftover sauce.

title: West African Chicken and Peanut Stew
blurb: Bone-in thighs braised until falling apart in a burnished peanut-tomato gravy with sweet potato and a hum of habanero heat that builds with every spoonful.

ingredients.item: 3/4 cup Simply Nature creamy peanut butter
6 garlic cloves and a 2-inch knob of ginger, both grated
1 habanero chile, halved (seeds removed for less heat)
1 lb sweet potatoes, cut in 1-inch cubes

steps.text: Pat the thighs very dry and season all over with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high until it just starts to smoke, then lay the thighs in skin side down in two batches.
steps.tip: Dry skin is the difference between browning and steaming.

steps.text: Sear without touching them until the skin is deep golden and lifts cleanly from the pot, then flip for one more minute and transfer to a plate. Pour off all but about 2 tbsp of the fat.
steps.tip: Let the skin release on its own.

steps.text: Drop the heat to medium and add the onions with a pinch of salt, scraping the browned bits off the bottom as they release moisture. Cook until they collapse and turn soft and translucent with golden edges.
steps.tip: Those stuck-on bits are pure flavor.

steps.text: Stir in the garlic, ginger, curry powder, and tomato paste and cook until the paste darkens from bright red to brick and smells toasty. Whisk the peanut butter into 1 cup of the broth in a measuring cup while this happens.
steps.tip: Pre-thinning the peanut butter stops it from clumping.

steps.text: Pour in the crushed tomatoes, the remaining broth, and the thinned peanut butter, then add the habanero halves and 1 1/2 tsp salt. Return the chicken and any juices to the pot, nestling the pieces so they are mostly submerged.
Bring to a bare simmer, cover partially, and let it bubble gently, stirring every 10 minutes so the peanut butter doesn't catch on the bottom. The stew should barely blip, not boil.
steps.tip: A hard boil will make the sauce break and turn greasy.

steps.text: Add the sweet potatoes and simmer uncovered until they are tender at the center of a knife tip and the sauce has darkened and thickened enough to coat a spoon. Fish out and discard the habanero.
steps.tip: Taste before removing the chile if you want more heat.

steps.text: Stir in the spinach in handfuls until it wilts into the gravy, then taste and adjust with salt. Heat the rice pouches and serve the stew ladled over rice in wide bowls.
steps.tip: The stew tastes even better the next day.

swap: Bone-in thighs unavailable? Use 2 1/2 lb boneless thighs and cut the covered simmer to 20 minutes.
leftovers: Keeps 4 days refrigerated and freezes beautifully for 3 months; loosen with a splash of broth when reheating since the peanut butter tightens as it chills.

title: Sri Lankan Devilled Chicken
blurb: Sticky, sweet-hot chicken tossed at high heat with onion wedges and green pepper until the sauce reduces to a clinging red lacquer perfumed with cinnamon.

ingredients.item: 1 1/4 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs (Kirkwood), cut in 1-inch strips
1 large red onion, cut in thick wedges and separated
1 green bell pepper, cut in 1-inch squares
4 garlic cloves and 1 tbsp grated ginger

steps.text: Toss the chicken strips with the curry powder, pepper flakes, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tbsp oil until every piece is rust colored. Let it sit on the counter while you cut the vegetables.
steps.tip: Room-temperature chicken sears instead of steams.

steps.text: Stir the sriracha, tomato paste, soy sauce, sugar, and 3 tbsp water into a smooth devilled sauce and park it by the stove. Start the rice packets in the microwave so they are ready at the end.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over high until it ripples and a strip of onion sizzles instantly. Add the cinnamon stick and let it toast until it smells sweet and woody.
steps.tip: The cinnamon perfumes the oil, so don't skip it.

steps.text: Spread the chicken in one layer and leave it completely alone until the underside is browned and crusted, then stir and cook until no pink remains on the outside.
steps.tip: Resist stirring early or you'll pull out water.

steps.text: Add the onion wedges and green pepper and stir-fry over high heat until they blister in spots but still have a distinct bite in the middle.
steps.tip: You want char, not softness.

steps.text: Add the garlic and ginger, toss for 30 seconds until fragrant, then pour in the devilled sauce. Toss constantly as it bubbles and reduces until it clings to the chicken and there is almost no liquid pooling in the pan.
steps.tip: Stop when the spoon leaves a clear trail.

steps.text: Pull out the cinnamon stick, taste for salt and heat, and serve over the hot jasmine rice while the sauce is still glossy.

swap: No Fusia sriracha? Trader Joe's Green Dragon Hot Sauce plus 1 extra tsp sugar gives a similar sweet-hot balance.
leftovers: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat in a hot dry skillet and tuck into L'Oven Fresh protein wraps with shredded cabbage.

title: Shoyu Ahi Poke Bowls
blurb: Cold cubes of ahi slicked in soyaki and sesame oil over warm jasmine rice, with sweet onion, avocado, and a spicy mayo drizzle that ties it all together.

ingredients.item: 12 oz ahi tuna steaks, thawed and very cold
1 Persian cucumber, sliced into thin coins
2 tsp Everything But The Bagel Sesame Seasoning

steps.text: Soak the shaved sweet onion in a bowl of ice water while you work so it loses its raw bite and turns crisp. Drain it well right before serving.
steps.tip: Ice water tames sharp onion in minutes.

steps.text: Pat the tuna completely dry and cut it against the grain into clean 3/4-inch cubes with a sharp knife, working quickly so the fish stays cold. Discard any tough silver sinew.
steps.tip: Partially frozen tuna cubes far more neatly.

steps.text: Toss the tuna gently with the Island Soyaki, sesame oil, and half the scallions using a spoon rather than your hands. Cover and refrigerate so it marinates without curing.
steps.tip: Any longer and the soy starts firming the fish.

steps.text: Microwave the jasmine rice packets per the package, fluff with a fork, and divide between two wide bowls. Let the rice cool for a couple of minutes so it doesn't cook the fish on contact.
steps.tip: Warm rice with cold fish is the classic contrast.

steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise and sriracha together with 1 tsp water until it is thin enough to drizzle from a spoon. Slice the avocado and cucumber while it sits.
Mound the marinated tuna over the rice and arrange the avocado, cucumber, and drained sweet onion around it in distinct sections. Pour any marinade left in the bowl over the rice.
steps.tip: Sections look better and let you build each bite.

steps.text: Zigzag the spicy mayo over the top, then finish with the remaining scallions, the Everything But The Bagel seasoning, and crumbled seaweed. Serve immediately while the fish is still cold.

swap: No sushi-grade ahi? Sear the tuna 45 seconds a side over blazing heat, or use two drained cans of Northern Catch solid tuna and skip the marinating step.
leftovers: Poke is best the day it is made; eat any leftovers within 24 hours or gently sear the cubes in a hot pan and fold them into fried rice.

title: Kielbasa and Caraway Cabbage with Mustard Cream
blurb: Browned coins of smoked kielbasa and crisped bacon over sweet-sour caraway cabbage and potatoes, all pulled together with a tangy mustard sour cream and a shower of dill.

ingredients.item: 14 oz Never Any! smoked Polish sausage, cut in 1/2-inch coins
1/2 head green cabbage, cored and shredded

steps.text: Put the halved potatoes in a microwave-safe bowl with 2 tbsp water, cover, and microwave until a knife slides into one with only slight resistance. Drain them and leave them uncovered so the surfaces dry.
steps.tip: Par-cooking here is what keeps this under 35 minutes.

steps.text: Cook the bacon in a large cold skillet over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the fat has rendered and the pieces are crisp and curled. Scoop the bacon out with a slotted spoon and leave the fat in the pan.
steps.tip: Starting cold renders the fat more completely.

steps.text: Turn the heat to medium-high and lay the kielbasa coins flat in the bacon fat. Sear undisturbed until the cut faces are dark brown and slightly domed, flip once, then move them to the bacon plate.
steps.tip: Flat contact is what builds the crust.

steps.text: Add the drained potatoes cut side down to the same pan and let them sit still until the flat sides are deeply golden and crusty. Push them to the edge of the pan.
steps.tip: Don't stir, or you'll get pale potatoes.

steps.text: Add the onion, caraway seeds, and paprika to the center and stir for a minute until the seeds smell toasted, then pile in the cabbage with 1 tsp salt. It will look like too much; press it down and let it wilt.
steps.tip: Cabbage loses half its volume almost immediately.

steps.text: Cook the cabbage, tossing every couple of minutes, until it is silky and browned in patches but still has some structure. Splash in the vinegar and sugar and scrape the bottom of the pan clean.
steps.tip: The vinegar deglazes and brightens all at once.

steps.text: Whisk the mustard and sour cream together with a splash of water and a grind of pepper until pourable. Return the sausage and bacon to the pan and toss just long enough to heat through.
Divide between two plates, spoon the mustard cream over the top rather than stirring it in, and finish with a heavy scatter of dill.
steps.tip: Sour cream added off heat stays smooth instead of splitting.

swap: No fresh dill? Use 2 tsp dried dill stirred into the sour cream, plus a squeeze of lemon at the end.
leftovers: Keeps 4 days refrigerated and reheats best in a skillet; fry leftovers with a couple of eggs cracked on top for breakfast.

title: Burmese Coconut Chicken Noodle Bowls
blurb: A golden turmeric-coconut chicken broth thickened to a velvet gravy, ladled over rice noodles and loaded with hard-boiled egg, crispy onions, and lime.

ingredients.item: 2 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs (Kirkwood), cut in 1-inch pieces
8 garlic cloves and a 2-inch knob of ginger

steps.text: Blitz the onions, garlic, and ginger in a food processor with a splash of water until you have a coarse, wet paste. If you have no processor, grate the ginger and garlic and mince the onion very fine.
steps.tip: This paste is the backbone of the broth.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium heat, add the onion paste and turmeric, and cook, stirring often, until the mixture darkens to a deep gold and the raw onion smell is gone. It should look jammy and pull away from the bottom.
steps.tip: Rushing this step leaves the broth tasting sharp.

steps.text: While the paste cooks, lower the eggs into a saucepan of boiling water and set a timer. Cook them, then shock them in ice water, peel, and halve.
steps.tip: Ice water makes the shells slip right off.

steps.text: Season the chicken with 1 tsp salt, add it to the onion paste, and stir over medium-high heat until the pieces are coated in gold and no longer pink on the outside.
steps.tip: You are coating, not browning.

steps.text: Pour in the broth, one can of the coconut milk, and the fish sauce. Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat so the surface just shivers and cook uncovered until the chicken is tender enough to shred against the side of the pot.
steps.tip: A gentle simmer keeps the coconut milk from breaking.

steps.text: Whisk the cornstarch into the second can of coconut milk until completely smooth, then stir it into the pot. Simmer, stirring, until the broth thickens into a silky gravy that coats the back of a spoon.
steps.tip: Whisk before pouring or you'll get lumps.

steps.text: Cook the rice noodles in a separate pot of salted water according to the package until just tender, then drain and rinse briefly with cool water so they don't clump.
steps.tip: Rinsing stops the noodles from soaking up all your broth.

steps.text: Taste the broth and adjust with fish sauce, salt, and a squeeze of lime until it is savory and bright. Nest noodles in each bowl, ladle the chicken and gravy over, and top with egg halves, crispy fried onions, and lime wedges.
steps.tip: Add the crispy onions at the table so they stay crunchy.

swap: No fish sauce? Use 3 tbsp Fusia soy sauce plus an extra squeeze of lime for the same savory-sour lift.
leftovers: Store the broth and noodles in separate containers for up to 4 days; the gravy thickens as it chills, so loosen it with broth or water when reheating.
